workloads.array: one list<int32> cell with size elements
workloads.nested: one nested list containing size int32 elements
workloads.string: one string repeating Unicode alpha, backslash and newline size times
workloads.sentinel: show(n=0) on one list<int32> cell with size elements
workloads.wide: size int32 columns and16rows; show one row

validation: 52 public Python show/convenience/native-memory tests passed after strict incremental UTF8 hardening.
Escaped Unicode and nested visible prefixes, logical values, parent validity with hidden Arrow children, sentinel/zero-field rows, ASCII wrapping and numeric alignment verified.
limitations: Each workload runs in a fresh subprocess, after runtime initialization and source construction;15second cap. RSS is whole-process peak on macOS including input buffers, not isolated display allocation.

Budget-proportional localization/rendering applies to ordinary strings and recursive array/set/dict/tuple/struct cells. Full native execution and source data construction are not made budget-proportional.
Locus/Call atoms retain prepared logical conversion and validation. Compound interval endpoints retain logical-converter/repr fallback, which can fully localize a large endpoint.

Nullable integer ndarray compatibility fallback can fully localize before its prior conversion/error behavior. Ordinary numeric ndarray uses Arrow-backed NumPy storage; rendering obeys existing NumPy print settings, and a user-set very large print threshold can still render a large representation before truncation.
Set enumeration now follows canonical native storage order instead of constructing a Python set; enumeration order is unspecified, spellings/content retained.
Remaining native/schema execution costs can dominate wide-table display; no claim of linear end-to-end cost for arbitrary schema width.
